name: Amnon
description: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Amnon fell sick with lust for his sister Tamar, and Jonadab, a subtle friend, gave him the devil's counsel to feign sickness and get her alone; the counsellor who is supposed to give godly counsel can tell you how to be the devil.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

points: Absalom the son of David had a fair sister named Tamar, and Amnon the son of David loved her, and was so vexed for her that he fell sick, for she was a virgin and he thought it hard to do anything to her. Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother, who was a very subtle man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Tamar went to Amnon's house, took flour, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight and baked them, but he refused to eat and commanded every man out from him. Then he told Tamar to bring the meat into the chamber that he might eat of her hand, and when she brought it, he took hold of her and said, Come lie with me, my sister.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: When King David heard all these things he was very wroth. And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had forced his sister Tamar.
David was upset at what happened to Tamar but did not do anything about it. Absalom said nothing to Amnon, but he was quietly holding on to the offense, waiting.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom told them to wait until Amnon was drunk and merry with wine, then to strike, and killed him for what he did to Tamar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: Absalom commanded his servants to mark when Amnon's heart was merry with wine, and when he gave the word to smite and kill him, to fear not, for he had commanded them. The servants did as Absalom commanded, and all the king's sons arose, every man got upon his mule, and fled.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: While they were on the way, tidings came to David that Absalom had slain all the king's sons and not one was left. The king arose, tare his garments, and lay on the earth. But Jonadab said not to suppose all were slain, for Amnon only was dead; by the appointment of Absalom this had been determined from the day Amnon forced his sister Tamar.
The report was exaggerated, so David thought all his sons were dead. Jonadab corrected him: only Amnon was dead, and it was because of what Amnon had done to Tamar.

note.label: 2 Samuel 13: Amnon Forces Tamar and Absalom Slays Amnon

points: The sons born to David in Hebron are named, from Amnon the firstborn to the sixth, with their mothers.
Amnon was the son who defiled his sister Tamar, and Absalom, named here among the younger sons, later avenged her and paid for it with his own life.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah
